Google has launched an experimental platform called Playground, where users can create a game based on a text description. Users formulate their idea, follow prompts, and receive a ready project. They can publish it on the platform for everyone to see or share it via a link.

The platform is currently only available to users in the US who are over 18 years old. The option to create their own games is gradually being opened up: although users can access the site from the US, not everyone has the ability to create a game. However, projects that have already been published can be viewed by all.

In the future, Playground is planned to be integrated with Unity Spark, an artificial intelligence-based agent for game development on the Unity engine.

🏦 South Korea's First Bitcoin-Backed Bank Loans Are Here

Jeonbuk Bank has quietly made history, launching South Korea's first bank-issued won loans backed by Bitcoin. Corporate clients can now pledge their BTC holdings as collateral for business financing — no selling required.

The structure keeps the bank at arm's length from the crypto itself: registered third-party custodians hold the collateral while Jeonbuk supplies the won, never taking ownership of the pledged assets. The program is currently corporate-only, with expansion contingent on regulatory shifts and market demand.

The obvious question hanging over the whole thing: what happens when BTC drops 30% overnight? The bank's collateral monitoring and valuation framework will face that test eventually.

Spain exempts self-custody wallets from crypto tax reporting

Spain's tax authorities have confirmed that cryptocurrency held in self-custody wallets — where the owner controls the private keys — does not need to be reported under Form 721, the country's disclosure form for foreign-held digital assets. The exemption hinges on one condition: no third party holds the assets on your behalf.

The rule draws a clean line between personal custody and exchange or custodial holdings abroad, which remain reportable. Simple in principle, potentially significant in practice — Spain just gave self-custody a regulatory edge.

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

A few dozen pools can only capture a few dozen tokens' worth of flow. Imagine this same efficient arbitrage engine running across hundreds of pools that simply don't exist yet.

The Takeaway:

The traders are ready. The volume is real. The arbitrage engine is already running. What's missing is the liquidity to serve that volume and capture those fees across a much broader range of pairs.
